name: Belotero Balance

lead: Belotero Balance is a soft hyaluronic acid filler from Merz used for fine lines, folds and the hollow under the eyes. People choose it for a smoother, brighter-looking area soon after injection.

Its cohesive polydensified matrix spreads evenly in the skin and adds subtle volume, then degrades over time. A split-face randomized comparison of three HA formulations for nasolabial folds followed patients for 12 months, and trials cover darker skin types and under-eye hollows. It is studied for lines and hollows rather than structural projection, and forum posters also discuss filler as a precursor or stand-in for surgery.

paras: A licensed clinician injects fine lines or the under-eye area in an office visit with little downtime. People repeat treatments as the gel absorbs, and it can be dissolved with hyaluronidase.
Filler complications across the category include bruising, nodules and rare vascular events. It is a prescription medical device, and results are temporary.

forums.title: How is Belotero as a filler option, good or nah?

chain: Soft cohesive HA integrates in skin
angle.text: Belotero Balance is a soft hyaluronic acid filler used for fine lines and under-eye hollows, giving a smoother, brighter-looking area soon after injection. The cohesive gel blends into the skin to fill shadow and lines. A 12-month randomized comparison exists for nasolabial folds.

lead: Belotero Balance is a hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler from Merz that uses cohesive polydensified matrix (CPM) technology, a gel designed to spread evenly and integrate smoothly into the skin. People use it to soften fine lines, smooth superficial folds such as the nasolabial folds, and fill the under-eye (infraorbital) hollow, so the face looks smoother, more rested and more even. [1][2][3]

The product belongs to the Belotero range, which also includes Basic, Soft, Intense, Hydro and Volume versions for different depths and areas. A 2016 literature review of the CPM filler family covered 26 papers and reported greater nasolabial fold improvement than bovine collagen in a randomized trial of 118 people, with an effect still visible at 8 to 12 months in many patients. [1]

Published studies include a split-face randomized comparison of three HA formulations for nasolabial folds with 12-month follow-up, trials in darker skin types, and a randomized comparison for the infraorbital hollow. [4][5][6][7] Because it is an injectable medical device, it is administered by licensed clinicians. Forum users who talk about it tend to ask whether filler can replace or precede surgery, a question the published studies do not address. [8]

paras: A literature review describes the CPM gel family and its use for soft-tissue augmentation and rejuvenation. The authors describe the gel as monophasic, meaning it is one continuous gel instead of particles suspended in a carrier, with variable density of HA that allows it to distribute homogeneously in tissue. [1]

A 2015 article on fine lines describes Belotero Balance as having low elasticity and viscosity, high cohesivity and high tan delta, properties the author links to a soft gel that flows into fine lines and tolerates movement in mobile areas of the face. The same article reports that ultrastructural analysis showed no detectable particles, which the author says minimises the bluish Tyndall effect that can occur with superficial filler. [9]

Laboratory studies rank fillers by cohesivity and rheology and place Belotero Balance among FDA-approved HA fillers evaluated. [10][11][12] Wikipedia's overview of dermal fillers notes that HA is the most common filler material, that many HA fillers are crosslinked with BDDE, and that in the United States fillers are regulated as medical devices that a provider must prescribe and perform. [13]

Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring sugar that binds water and swells into a gel, and crosslinked HA gels injected as dermal fillers typically last about six to twelve months, with products differing in crosslinking method and gel behaviour [14]. Belotero Balance is positioned at the soft, superficial end of the range, in contrast with firmer gels designed to add projection to the cheeks or chin [1][9]. Wikipedia lists vascular occlusion, bruising and nodules among possible HA filler complications [14].

Merz's US site lists three products in the line, each with a lidocaine-containing (+) version. Belotero Balance (+) is labelled for smoothing moderate to severe facial wrinkles and folds such as the nasolabial folds, and for adding volume beneath the eyes in adults over 21. Belotero Volume (+) is labelled for restoring midface volume and cheek fullness in adults 22 or older, and Belotero Intense (+) for adding lip volume in adults over 21 [15].

Merz states that results from Balance (+) and Volume (+) can last up to 18 months and from Intense (+) up to 12 months, and notes that among Balance (+) patients who saw results by week 8, about 90% (20 patients) still did at 72 weeks; it adds that safety and effectiveness beyond 96 weeks for Balance (+) are not known [15]. Published reviews describe the effect in nasolabial folds as still visible at 8 to 12 months [1].

The product is prescription-only, and the manufacturer's prescribing information lists patient groups for whom it is not intended, including people with severe allergies involving anaphylaxis, allergy to lidocaine-type anaesthetics, or a tendency to form keloids [15].

Belotero is made by Merz, a family-owned German company founded in Frankfurt in 1908 by the pharmacist and chemist Friedrich Merz. Its Merz Aesthetics division, formed in late 2019 and headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, also markets Xeomin botulinum toxin, the Ultherapy ultrasound device and the Radiesse biostimulator [16]. Wikipedia reports that Merz bought the Swiss dermal filler maker Anteis in 2013 [16], and the literature review treats Esthelis, Mesolis, Fortelis and Modelis as equivalent products to the Belotero fillers [1].

The 2015 review of CPM HA for fine lines frames the product as suited to intradermal, superficial placement, and reports evidence-level II data for efficacy and for longevity of up to a year or more. [9] Registered trials cover nasolabial folds, facial wrinkles and etched-in fine lines. [5][17][18]

The infraorbital hollow is a concavity between the lower eyelid and cheek that can make a person look tired. A systematic review of fillers for tear trough rejuvenation, which includes Belotero among the products searched, notes substantial variation in treatment parameters and the importance of anatomy and product choice. [19] A multicenter, evaluator-blind, randomized, controlled study of Belotero Balance (+), a version with lidocaine, was published in 2024 for correcting infraorbital hollowing in adults. [7]

Belotero products have been studied in the lip and perioral area. A 2012 technique article on lip enhancement is cited in the literature on these products, [2] a registered trial compared Restylane Silk with Belotero Balance for perioral lines, [20] and a multicenter randomized trial compared four HA fillers for lip augmentation head-to-head. [21]

A 2013 review of key Belotero Balance trials reports two pivotal studies showing non-inferiority and superiority to bovine collagen. In the first, more than half of patients maintained optimal correction at 6 months on the Belotero side of the face. The second followed patients to week 96 in an open-label design, and effects persisted in the majority of subjects without repeat treatment for at least one interval of 48 weeks. A third study compared Belotero with Juvederm and Restylane and reported comparable safety and similar aesthetic results. [22]

The 2016 review summarised three randomized controlled trials: greater reduction in nasolabial fold severity than collagen (n=118, at 8 to 24 weeks), than Restylane at 4 weeks (n=40), and higher patient satisfaction than Perlane for Belotero Intense at 2 weeks (n=20). It reports that about 80 percent of patients improved by at least one point on a severity scale 1 to 6 months after injection. [1] A rater-blind randomized comparison of Belotero Basic and Restylane for nasolabial folds is also published. [23]

The 12-month split-face study randomised 40 participants: 20 received Belotero in one nasolabial fold and Restylane in the other, and 20 received Belotero in one fold and Juvederm in the other. Mean severity was 2.3 before treatment and about 1.5 to 1.6 at 12 months, the three products produced essentially equivalent results, and participants tended, without statistical significance, to prefer Belotero; the 4-week evenness rating favoured Belotero [4]. The 2013 review also cites a five-year retrospective safety review of 317 treated patients that reported no severe adverse events and no persistent nodules or granulomas [22].

Under-eye results. In the 2024 randomised, evaluator-blind trial of Belotero Balance (+) for infraorbital hollowing, eligible adults with moderate or severe hollowing were randomised 2:1 to treatment or an untreated control group that was treated after week 8. At week 8 the estimated response rate, defined as at least one point of improvement on the Merz Infraorbital Hollow Assessment Scale, was 80.6% in treated patients and 1.9% in controls, and 88 of 97 responders (90.7%) retained improvement 48 weeks after treatment; no unexpected adverse events were reported [7].

Fine lines. The 2015 review of CPM filler for fine lines describes the gel as having low elasticity and viscosity with high cohesivity, and the author argues this lets it be placed superficially in mobile areas while moving with the skin [9]. The 2016 review also reports a magnetic resonance study showing no loss of Belotero Volume at 12 months and positive findings for Soft and Hydro versions [1].

Hyaluronic acid fillers can be degraded with the enzyme hyaluronidase, which is a feature of the category. In-vitro studies have examined how Belotero and other commercial HA fillers respond to hyaluronidase, and they found that products differ in how readily they are broken down. [24][25] A 2023 study tested the response of 21 HA fillers to recombinant human hyaluronidase, [26] and a randomized trial examined the kinetics of reversing HA filler with hyaluronidase. [27]

The 2023 laboratory study placed 0.2 mL samples of 21 HA fillers on slides and added recombinant human hyaluronidase at intervals over three hours. It placed Belotero Balance in the moderately resistant group on the less resistant side, Belotero Intense in the moderately resistant group, and Belotero Volume among the most resistant fillers, and reported that most fillers on the market were quite resistant to the enzyme [26]. Reversal is carried out by clinicians, and the authors say the findings bear on managing both ischemic and nonischemic complications [26].

Reviews of injectable fillers describe adverse events as typically mild: injection pain, redness, swelling and bruising. Asymmetry, nodules, ptosis and intravascular occlusion are less common. [3] In the 2013 review of Belotero Balance trials, only one of 34 adverse events (injection-site bruising) was judged related to the device. [22]

Analyses of FDA adverse-event reports and litigation, and a cross-sectional study of complications and lawsuits involving injectable facial fillers, describe vascular and other complications for fillers as a category. [28][29] Wikipedia notes that blindness from embolisation into the ophthalmic and retinal arteries is a rare serious complication of filler injection and that vision loss is usually permanent when it occurs. [13] The under-eye area is described in the tear trough review as an unforgiving region where anatomy knowledge matters. [19]

Manufacturer safety information lists swelling, bruising, redness, pain and lumps as common side effects that usually resolve within one to four weeks, delayed-onset inflammation that can follow infections, vaccinations or dental procedures, and the rare but serious risk of unintentional injection into a blood vessel, which can cause vision problems, stroke and permanent scarring [15]. The label does not recommend injecting areas with active skin infection, cold sores or rashes until healed, and safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established [15].

The 2016 literature review reported mild to moderate erythema, oedema and haematoma as the most common effects and noted no reports of Tyndall effect, nodules or granulomas in the reviewed papers [1]. The tear trough review reports patient satisfaction as high with effects lasting 8 to 12 months, and describes injection technique varying between clinicians [19].

A prospective split-face randomized study compared three HA formulations for nasolabial folds over 12 months. [4] A literature review summarises CPM filler studies, including three randomized trials against collagen, Restylane and Perlane. [1] A review of key Belotero Balance trials covers the pivotal collagen comparisons and a 96-week open-label follow-up. [22]

Registered trials include a pivotal multicenter study of Belotero in facial wrinkles (n=118, started 2006), a study of Belotero Soft (n=64, 2007), a study in Fitzpatrick skin types IV-VI (n=93, 2009), a post-approval nasolabial fold study (n=117, 2012), a lidocaine pain study (n=52, 2017), a midface fullness scale study (n=66, 2017), an infraorbital hollow pilot (n=66, 2018), and comparisons in perioral lines with Restylane Silk (n=50). [5][6][17][20][30][31][32][33]
A 2023 review of combined calcium hydroxyapatite and HA fillers, which includes Belotero Volume, reported greater skin remodelling with sequential than with simultaneous injection. [34]

Summary of designs. The 2012 split-face study (n=40) and the 2024 under-eye trial are randomised and controlled; the 2016 review pooled three randomised comparisons against collagen (n=118), Restylane (n=40) and Perlane (n=20); and the 2013 review adds a 96-week open-label follow-up and a retrospective review of 317 patients [1][4][7][22].

Belotero sits in the same market as Juvederm and Restylane, and head-to-head studies commonly use them as comparators [4][22]. In looksmaxxing forums, soft-tissue fillers are generally discussed alongside surgery as a non-surgical option, and the Belotero thread asks whether it is a sensible filler to try before a major procedure [8]. The product's labelled indications concern lines, folds, under-eye volume, midface volume and lips, rather than bone structure [15].

claims.claim: Filler can stand in for or precede major surgery
Belotero gives a natural, subtle result in the under-eye area.
HA filler can be dissolved if the result is unwanted.
Results last a year or more.
Filler is a low-risk way to change the face.
